REPLACE-CHECK

The check passes today with `-W error::DeprecationWarning`, yet the second transcript clearly shows the warnings are still present (2 warnings emitted). This means the check does not discriminate—it reports success whether or not the work is done. The issue is that pytest's `-W error::DeprecationWarning` flag apparently isn't converting these specific `pty.py` warnings into failures on this platform/configuration. A valid check needs to explicitly detect the warning count, such as `uv run pytest tests/test_terminals.py tests/web/test_terminal_ws.py -q 2>&1 | grep -c "DeprecationWarning"` returning 0, or a more robust approach that actually fails when warnings are present.
